claim: OpenAI's Preparedness Framework v2 has three Tracked Categories of frontier capability: Biological and Chemical, Cybersecurity, and AI Self-improvement.

source.excerpt: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories: Biological and Chemical capabilities... Cybersecurity capabilities... AI Self-improvement capabilities

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 2, Introduction. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI defines 'severe harm' as the death or grave injury of thousands of people or hundreds of billions of dollars of economic damage.

source.excerpt: By 'severe harm' in this document, we mean the death or grave injury of thousands of people or hundreds of billions of dollars of economic damage.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 2 footnote 1. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI defines 'High' capability thresholds as capabilities that significantly increase existing risk vectors for severe harm, and 'Critical' as capabilities that present a meaningful risk of a qualitatively new threat vector.

source.excerpt: High capability thresholds mean capabilities that significantly increase existing risk vectors for severe harm... Critical capability thresholds mean capabilities that present a meaningful risk of a qualitatively new threat vector for severe harm with no ready precedent.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 4, Tracked Categories. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: A frontier capability is tracked only if the risk it creates meets five criteria: plausible, measurable, severe, net new, and instantaneous or irremediable.

source.excerpt: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria: 1. Plausible... 2. Measurable... 3. Severe... 4. Net new... 5. Instantaneous or irremediable

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 4, Tracked Categories. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Cybersecurity [High] threshold is reached when the model removes existing bottlenecks to scaling cyber operations by automating end-to-end cyber operations against reasonably hardened targets OR by automating the discovery and exploitation of operationally relevant vulnerabilities.

source.excerpt: [High] The model removes existing bottlenecks to scaling cyber operations including by automating end-to-end cyber operations against reasonably hardened targets OR by automating the discovery and exploitation of operationally relevant vulnerabilities.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 5, Table 1 — Tracked Categories (Cybersecurity High). URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Cybersecurity [Critical] threshold is reached when a tool-augmented model can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention OR can devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks against hardened targets.

source.excerpt: [Critical] A tool-augmented model can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention OR model can devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks against hardened targets given only a high level desired goal.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 7, Table 1 — Tracked Categories (Cybersecurity Critical). URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Biological and Chemical [High] threshold is reached when the model can provide meaningful counterfactual assistance to 'novice' actors that enables them to create known biological or chemical threats.

source.excerpt: [High] The model can provide meaningful counterfactual assistance (relative to unlimited access to baseline of tools available in 2021) to 'novice' actors (anyone with a basic relevant technical background) that enables them to create known biological or chemical threats.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 5, Table 1 — Tracked Categories (Bio/Chem High). URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Biological and Chemical [Critical] threshold is reached when the model can enable an expert to develop a highly dangerous novel threat vector (e.g., comparable to a novel CDC Class A biological agent).

source.excerpt: [Critical] The model can enable an expert to develop a highly dangerous novel threat vector (e.g., comparable to a novel CDC Class A biological agent) OR the model can be connected to tools and equipment to complete the full engineering and/or synthesis cycle of a regulated or novel biological threat without human intervention.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 6, Table 1 — Tracked Categories (Bio/Chem Critical). URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's AI Self-improvement [Critical] threshold is reached when the model is capable of recursively self-improving, defined as either a superhuman research-scientist agent OR causing a generational model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equivalent 2024 progress.

source.excerpt: [Critical] The model is capable of recursively self improving (i.e., fully automated AI R&D), defined as either (leading indicator) a superhuman research-scientist agent OR (lagging indicator) causing a generational model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equivalent progress in 2024 (e.g., sped up to just 4 weeks) sustainably for several months.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 7, Table 1 — Tracked Categories (AI Self-improvement Critical). URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Preparedness Framework v2 has five Research Categories: Long-range Autonomy, Sandbagging, Autonomous Replication and Adaptation, Undermining Safeguards, and Nuclear and Radiological.

source.excerpt: These include Long-range Autonomy, Sandbagging, Autonomous Replication and Adaptation, Undermining Safeguards, and Nuclear and Radiological.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 7-8, Table 2 — Research Categories. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI removed Persuasion from the Preparedness Framework in v2, moving it to the Model Spec and Usage Policy instead — because Persuasion risks do not meet the framework's severe-harm definition.

source.excerpt: Going forward we will handle risks related to persuasion outside the Preparedness Framework, including via our Model Spec and policy prohibitions on the use of our tools for political campaigning or lobbying... Persuasion category risks do not fit the criteria for inclusion.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 9, Persuasion removed to Research/Outside. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Safety Advisory Group (SAG) is a cross-functional group of OpenAI leaders that oversees the Preparedness Framework; OpenAI Leadership can approve or reject SAG recommendations, and the Board's Safety and Security Committee provides oversight.

source.excerpt: An internal, cross-functional group of OpenAI leaders called the Safety Advisory Group (SAG) oversees the Preparedness Framework and makes expert recommendations on the level and type of safeguards required for deploying frontier capabilities safely and securely. OpenAI Leadership can approve or reject these recommendations, and our Board's Safety and Security Committee provides oversight of these decisions.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 3, §1.1. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: OpenAI will adjust its safeguards downward only if it assesses doing so does not meaningfully increase overall severe-harm risk, publicly acknowledges the adjustment, and keeps safeguards more protective than the other AI developer's.

source.excerpt: If we are able to rigorously confirm that such a scenario has occurred, then we could adjust accordingly the level of safeguards that we require in that capability area, but only if: we assess that doing so does not meaningfully increase the overall risk of severe harm, we publicly acknowledge that we are making the adjustment, and, in order to avoid a race to the bottom on safety, we keep our safeguards at a level more protective than the other AI developer, and share information to validate this claim.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 12, §4.3 Marginal risk. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: AI Self-improvement was elevated from Research Category to Tracked Category in v2 because it presents a distinct plausible, net new, and potentially irremediable risk of hard-to-track rapid acceleration in AI capabilities.

source.excerpt: AI Self-improvement (now a Tracked Category), Long-range Autonomy and Autonomous Replication and Adaptation (now Research Categories) are distinct aspects of what we formerly termed Model Autonomy. We have separated self-improvement because it presents a distinct plausible, net new, and potentially irremediable risk, namely that of a hard-to-track rapid acceleration in AI capabilities which could have hard-to-predict severely harmful consequences.

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 7, Changes to Tracked Categories. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: GPT-5.4 Thinking is the first general-purpose model to have implemented mitigations for High capability in Cybersecurity under the Preparedness Framework.

source.excerpt: GPT‑5.4 Thinking is the latest reasoning model in the GPT‑5 series, and explained in our blog. The comprehensive safety mitigation approach for this model is similar to previous models in this series, but 5.4 Thinking is the first general purpose model to have implemented mitigations for High capability in Cybersecurity.

provenance.context: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card, Introduction. URL: https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-4-thinking/gpt-5-4-thinking.pdf

claim: OpenAI treats GPT-5.4-Thinking as High-cyber because it cannot rule out the capability — the model 'meets the requirements of each of our canary thresholds'.

source.excerpt: We are treating this model as High, even though we cannot be certain that it actually has these capabilities, because it meets the requirements of each of our canary thresholds and we therefore cannot rule out the possibility that it is in fact Cyber High.

provenance.context: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card, §5 Preparedness Framework. URL: https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-4-thinking/gpt-5-4-thinking.pdf

claim: OpenAI's cyber-incident analysis identifies three skills required for severe cyber harm: discovery of advanced operationally relevant exploits, goal-oriented end-to-end attack automation, and consistency in operations.

source.excerpt: In our analysis of prior cybersecurity incidents involving severe harm through either of these two routes, we find each instance demanded proficiency in each of three skills: 1. Discovery of advanced, operationally relevant exploits 2. Goal-oriented, end-to-end attack automation 3. Consistency in operations, allowing the attacker to scale damage and/or avoid discovery

provenance.context: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card, §5 Preparedness Framework. URL: https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-4-thinking/gpt-5-4-thinking.pdf

claim: OpenAI released an open-source 'CoT controllability' evaluation; GPT-5.4 Thinking's ability to deliberately obfuscate its reasoning is reported as low, which OpenAI frames as a positive safety property for CoT monitoring.

source.excerpt: We find that GPT‑5.4 Thinking's ability to control its CoT is low, which is a positive property for safety, suggesting that the model lacks the ability to hide its reasoning and that CoT monitoring remains an effective safety tool.

provenance.context: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card — CoT monitorability section. URL: https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-4-thinking/gpt-5-4-thinking.pdf

claim: GPT-5.4 is deployed under Trusted Access for Cyber (TAP) controls, with request-level blocking on ZDR surfaces and asynchronous monitoring — OpenAI also offers GPT-5.4-Cyber with reduced refusal boundaries for security professionals.

source.excerpt: These include an expanded cyber safety stack, including monitoring systems, trusted access controls, and asynchronous blocking for higher-risk requests for customers on Zero Data Retention (ZDR) surfaces, alongside ongoing investment in the broader security ecosystem.

provenance.context: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card + 'Introducing GPT-5.4' blog. URL: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-4/

claim: Sora 2 was released under Preparedness Framework v2.1 and did not trigger a capability threshold determination — its safeguards stack borrows from Sora 1, GPT-4o Image Generation, and DALL·E.

source.excerpt: Our iterative deployment includes rolling out initial access to Sora 2 via limited invitations, restricting the use of image uploads that feature a photorealistic person and all video uploads, and placing stringent safeguards and moderation thresholds on content involving minors.

provenance.context: Sora 2 System Card, Iterative Deployment. URL: https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/1759350502104.pdf

claim: OpenAI's Red Team Network conducted external testing on Sora 2 for content generation (sexual content, non-consensual likeness, misleading generations) and tested media-generation safeguards.

source.excerpt: OpenAI worked with external testers from OpenAI's Red Team Network to test Sora 2, evaluate existing safety mitigations, and provide feedback on emerging risks. Red teamers assessed new safety measures, and suggested improvements for future iterations.

provenance.context: Sora 2 System Card, Red Teaming. URL: https://www.rivista.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/1759350502104.pdf

claim: OpenAI's blog post on Astra states: 'we cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities under our Preparedness Framework' for the upcoming Astra model, prompting scaled-up robustness testing and security controls.

source.excerpt: Accordingly, we have scaled up robustness testing of our safeguards and security controls so that they are appropriate for a deployment of these capabilities.

provenance.context: OpenAI blog 'Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities'. URL: https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities/

claim: OpenAI's Astra blog states the Preparedness Framework 'has already guided us through other capability transitions' — including a June 2025 biology High determination — before the Astra cyber determination.

source.excerpt: The framework has already guided us through other capability transitions. In June 2025, as our models approached the high capability threshold for biology under the Preparedness Framework, we outlined the steps we were taking to strengthen safeguards, expand testing, work with external experts, and deploy additional security controls. We are applying the same principle here.

provenance.context: OpenAI blog 'Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities'. URL: https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities/

claim: Change-log item 4 in Preparedness Framework v2 states: 'Going forward we will handle risks related to persuasion outside the Preparedness Framework, including via our Model Spec and policy prohibitions on the use of our tools for political campaigning or lobbying.'

source.excerpt: Going forward we will handle risks related to persuasion outside the Preparedness Framework, including via our Model Spec and policy prohibitions on the use of our tools for political campaigning or lobbying, and our ongoing investigations of misuse of our products (including detecting and disrupting influence operations).

provenance.context: Preparedness Framework v2, Page 14-15, Appendix A Change log item 4. URL: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf

claim: The Future of Life Institute's AI Safety Index Summer 2026 graded OpenAI 2.28 out of 4.0 (C), with OpenAI leading only the Risk Assessment domain (2.54).

source.excerpt: OpenAI | 2.28 | C | OpenAI leads Risk Assessment with a score of 2.54.

provenance.context: FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026, Scorecard. URL: https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index-summer-2026/

claim: FLI grades Existential Safety as the weakest domain industry-wide; Anthropic's D+ in Existential Safety is the best score any lab achieved in that domain.

source.excerpt: Existential Safety was the weakest category across the entire industry, with Anthropic's D+ being the best score any lab achieved in that domain.

provenance.context: FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026, domain commentary. URL: https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index-summer-2026/
